relevance_note: The paper is a retrospective study of anakinra in 47 patients with "autoinflammatory diseases (AID)" (SJIA, CAPS, MKD, SURF, PIMS-TS, Blau syndrome, PAPA, NLRC4-AID, polyarticular JIA); no TNFAIP3 variant, no A20 haploinsufficiency and no HA20 diagnosis is printed anywhere, so no person is in scope.
method_note: Read the paper, schema and rules; no other file opened. I searched the full text (including the reference list and the table) for 'TNFAIP3', 'A20', 'haploinsufficiency', 'HA20' and related terms and found no occurrence; the only genetic statement is 'Diagnosis of monogenic autoinflammatory diseases was confirmed by Sanger sequencing.' Table 1 is a group-level summary (diagnosis groups, counts, means) with no per-patient variant data, so no rows were transcribed and no script was used. No in-scope person exists (no TNFAIP3 variant, no HA20 diagnosis, and no relative of such a person), therefore reports_individuals_with_tnfaip3_variant is false, only the publications row is filled, and the other four tables are empty, per the instructions section 'When the paper describes no in-scope person'. Uncertainty: (1) cites_prior_report_of_same_patients - the paper cites reference 30 (Fingerhutova et al., Muckle-Wells syndrome across four generations in one Czech family) next to a statement about its own CAPS patients, but never states that any of its patients were described earlier, so I recorded null rather than true or false; prior_report_citation is therefore 'not reported'. (2) n_patients_reported is null because the authors state no number of patients with a TNFAIP3 variant; cohort_size_as_stated = 47 is the analysed study population, although the authors also mention 60 patients prescribed anakinra of whom 13 were excluded. No contradictions were found in the paper.
